import KitFacts from "../../../../../components/ui/KitFacts.astro";

The web components kit is `@polaris-key/elements`. It runs in any page, Angular, Vue, Svelte or htmx
app, with no framework of its own. Every catalog component is a `pk-*` element over the shared
headless layer, and draws the same DOM under the same stylesheet as the [React kit](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/react/),
so a state looks the same in both. The kit takes its product identity from the SDK. The package is
on the [feeds](/docs/build/install-from-feeds/) and its CDN module is served at
`https://key.plrs.im/elements/<version>/pk.js`.

<KitFacts kit="elements" />

## The two-line flow

Layer (a): `<pk-gate>` with a `config` starts itself. The module registers every element and adds
its own styles and fonts.

```html
<script type="module" src="https://key.plrs.im/elements/1/pk.js"></script>
<pk-gate config='{"product":"tidewater"}'><my-app></my-app></pk-gate>
```

From the package, `import "@polaris-key/elements"` is the script line.

### The CDN module

`/elements/1/pk.js` follows the current 1.x release, cached for five minutes: a fix reaches your
page within minutes, and you do not control when. To fix the bytes, name the exact version and pin its
hash. `integrity.json` beside `pk.js` lists the sha384 of every file:

```html
<script
  type="module"
  src="https://key.plrs.im/elements/1.0.0/pk.js"
  integrity="sha384-…"
  crossorigin="anonymous"
></script>
```

An exact-version URL is immutable, cached for a year, and its bytes never change. Do not put
`integrity` on the floating URL: its bytes change with each release and the browser refuses the
module. Before 1.0 the major is `0`, which is not stable: pin the exact version. A prerelease
(`-alpha`, `-beta`, `-rc`) is published at its exact version only; the floating major follows stable
releases. A build that was not stamped with a release version (`0.0.0`) is served `no-cache`.

The `integrity` attribute covers `pk.js` only. A browser does not check it on the modules `pk.js`
imports, and the locale packs are such modules (`chunks/*.js`). To verify the whole graph, add an
import map before the script. `integrity.json` carries it ready to paste, as `importMap`, with
every module's sha384 keyed by its URL:

```html
<script type="importmap">
  {
    "integrity": {
      "https://key.plrs.im/elements/1.0.0/pk.js": "sha384-…",
      "https://key.plrs.im/elements/1.0.0/chunks/en-….js": "sha384-…"
    }
  }
</script>
<script type="module" src="https://key.plrs.im/elements/1.0.0/pk.js"></script>
```

The map must come before any module loads. If the page already has an import map, merge
`integrity` into it: browsers before Chrome 133 accept only one map per page.

Import-map integrity needs a browser that supports it (Chrome and Edge 127 and later; check the
current table for Firefox and Safari). Where it is unsupported the map is ignored and only the
`integrity` attribute on `pk.js` protects the page, so keep the attribute as well. Fonts are data and
are not covered.

A page with a Content-Security-Policy allows the path, not the whole host:
`script-src https://key.plrs.im/elements/` and `font-src https://key.plrs.im/elements/`.
The route sends `access-control-allow-origin: *`, no cookie and no credentials.

The gate builds the browser client from `config`, and never shows sign-in while a cached session is
checked. It renders your app in its default slot once the license holds, under the grace banner
while offline grace runs. Until then it owns the window and runs Welcome, sign-in in the browser,
Use a license key, the device limit and the blocking states with their fixes (Try again,
Reconnect, Sign out). A device limit is a neutral callout whose one primary, Replace a device,
opens the license's page with the app's address and the typed key; the key is tried again when the
person comes back. Escape backs out of a step, and focus follows each new screen. When the product
publishes a newer build, an update dialog opens over the app with up to three lines from that
release's changelog entry, the version you have, and All changes. Every control also raises
`pk-action` on the gate.

| `config` member    | What it sets                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `product`          | The product's slug (required)                                                                |
| `baseUrl`          | The control-plane origin; default `https://key.plrs.im`                                      |
| `version`          | The app's version: reported with the device, and what the update dialog says you have        |
| `auth`             | `"cookie"`, `"bearer"` or `"auto"` (the default); a page on another origin signs in by token |
| `trust`            | `{ "pinnedKeys": {…} }`, the keys a bearer page verifies documents against                   |
| `expectedServices` | The services the app expects until the product answers                                       |
| `returnUrl`        | The app's address, added to the device-limit link as `return=`                               |

`config` wins over `input`; a bad config raises `pk-error` (`detail.code` is `invalid-options`) and
draws nothing.

A control only the host can answer draws only when the host says so. `handles` names them:
`trial`, `restore`, `continue-free` and `renew`. Without it Welcome offers Sign in and Use a license
key, and an expired license offers Use another license alone.

```html
<pk-gate config='{"product":"tidewater"}' handles="trial renew">…</pk-gate>
<script type="module">
  document.querySelector("pk-gate").addEventListener("pk-action", (e) => {
    if (e.detail.key === "welcome.trial") startTrial();
    if (e.detail.key === "status.renew") location.assign("/pricing");
  });
</script>
```

## Piecemeal

Layer (b): every catalog component is an element, `pk-welcome`, `pk-activate`, `pk-devices`,
`pk-settings`, `pk-update-prompt` and the rest of the [catalog](/docs/build/ui/). It draws the state
its `input` property describes (a `UiInput`: what your app knows now) and reports each control as
a `pk-action` event instead of calling the SDK.

| Property or event | What it does                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`           | The state to draw                                                                                          |
| `pk-action`       | A control was pressed: `detail.key` (its copy key), `detail.action`, `detail.component` and `detail.state` |
| `pk-input`        | The person typed in a field (`detail.field`, `detail.value`)                                               |
| `pk-select`       | The person picked a row: a device, a license                                                               |
| `bare`            | An embedded pane without its own frame                                                                     |
| `fill`            | A blocking screen that owns the window                                                                     |

```html
<pk-devices id="devices" bare></pk-devices>
<script type="module">
  const el = document.getElementById("devices");
  el.input = { devices: [{ id: "d1", name: "Studio Mac", current: true }] };
  el.addEventListener("pk-action", (e) => console.log(e.detail.key));
</script>
```

## The sign-in form

`pk-sign-in` is the one sign-in form. Its body morphs in place through the steps: the methods, the
browser hand-off or its code, the license choice, a license key, then Done. Set `presentation` to
`"inline"` (default), `"sheet"` (a modal dialog, a bottom sheet on a narrow window) or `"browser"`,
and `primitives` to the SDK's sign-in primitives; without them it draws its `input`.

## Styling and presentation

Theme the whole page with `PolarisKey.theme({ … })`, a subtree with `<pk-provider theme='{…}'>`, or
one element with its `theme` property; an inner layer wins over an outer one. When the theme leaves
them unset, the gate takes the product's name, accent and verified icon from the SDK. Colors, radii,
type and spacing are `--pk-*` variables; set the shape tokens (`--pk-font-sans`, `--pk-kit-radius-*`,
`--pk-kit-control-height`, `--pk-kit-focus-*`) once on `pk-provider` as `--pk-provider-<name>`, for
example `--pk-provider-kit-radius-card`, and every element inside reads them. Every part is a `::part` (`primary`, `secondary`, `card`, …)
carrying a `data-key`. The page's own CSS reaches the parts without `!important`:

```css
pk-gate::part(primary) {
  border-radius: 999px;
}
```

The theme's `poweredBy` (`PolarisKey.theme({ poweredBy: "line" })`) adds the Polaris Locker line at
the foot of the account pane and About; `"badge"` draws the 320 × 104 badge on About where 320 px are
free. Off by default; never on a gate.

A page with a Content-Security-Policy allows `img-src blob:` for the product's icon.

## Headless

Layer (c): `@polaris-key/elements/headless` re-exports ui-core's models. `viewOf(component, input)`
returns a component's `View`: its state, the copy keys it shows, the actions its controls perform and
its decisions. For the browser client and the gate's controller, `@polaris-key/ui-core/browser`
exports `createBrowserClient`, `GateDriver` and `parseGateConfig`, the module both web kits share.

## Sample

`examples/ui/elements/` is Tidewater Studio: `index.html` is the two lines, `play.html` runs the
same gate on fixtures with no Worker, and `states.html` indexes the gate's states and panes.
